[Subscribe to WelcomeStack](https://substack.com/redirect/c7df8345-5b28-4946-9df9-6d893f905e55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Three years ago, I was running for U.S. Congress in St. Louis.
When I started running, it was a true 50/50 district.1 I was lucky to have the support of voters, friends, local organizations, and national groups like [WelcomePAC](https://substack.com/redirect/5f3dbe5b-d096-4936-9d39-da67864d7951?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). By most objective measures, we ran a pretty good campaign.2
But in the [waning hours of the 2022 legislative session](https://substack.com/redirect/355db14a-8ba9-4e12-b5d5-73ecd2abb1dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the Republican-controlled legislature made the district about 10 points more Republican and, for good measure, [drew my house out of the district I was running in](https://substack.com/redirect/d511c3bd-d581-480e-9fe6-82424ee2dc7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by about a block.3
With no real path to winning, I couldn't in good faith ask people for more time, energy, money, and support.4 So I dropped out.5
I get asked a lot whether I'm likely to run for office again. There's a classic I-wouldn't-rule-anything-out attitude in politics,6 but with every year that goes by, it's less and less likely that I do it again.
**We need to find ways to make it easier for good people** 7**to run for office. Because right now, it 's brutally difficult--especially for the sorts of candidates whose profiles give them the best chance of winning hard races.**8
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=155936496&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTU1OTM2NDk2LCJpYXQiOjE3MzgxNjg4NjcsImV4cCI6MTc0MDc2MDg2NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ePvlBXRxW4gUp1yaSrtHqPF1u6yEfemwohWTGjJWSpM)
### **On a good day,**_**only**_**45% of people hate you**
You know that going in, and you know that you're not going to be able to please everyone. But what caught me by surprise:
* There are hundreds of people who commit a lot of time to the act of hating you. It doesn't matter that you know, intellectually, that the basement dwellers9 who spend 15 hours a day picking fights on social media [aren't even a little bit representative of the electorate](https://substack.com/redirect/5600a231-a5eb-4923-9b9e-a88e7ffd7eb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It's hard to not let that warp your worldview.
* I assumed that, running as a Democrat, most of the vitriol would come from the political right. Some did, but most came from the far left.10

I ran because, in a Republican-leaning district, I thought my background--as an unapologetic pragmatist--was a good fit for the district, and better than what we'd been getting:
1. I've voted for both Democrats and Republicans in my life. I came to the Democratic Party disheartened and dismayed by Trumpism, but not all Republican ideas are bad, and not all Republicans are morally bankrupt.
2. I've worked on both sides of the aisle, which is pretty unusual in this political moment.11

The most successful candidates--Representatives like [Marie Gluesenkamp Perez](https://substack.com/redirect/64d030fe-ecb9-4136-9023-a99bb0ff8a58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Jared Golden](https://substack.com/redirect/4953f4e3-4465-4270-b22e-44c2229e39a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who consistently win in Republican-leaning districts--do so by running this kind of campaign: independent-minded and focused on local issues.
To win in purple and red-leaning districts, Democrats have to meet voters where they are--and that very often means finding areas where you can differentiate yourself from an unpopular national brand. That's especially true right now: the [economy was the top issue for voters](https://substack.com/redirect/3bf38953-9fa9-4ab4-bf18-92a0e72b5818?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2024,12 and voters trusted Donald Trump on this issue considerably more than Kamala Harris.
So fighting among Democrats because your message is too politically inclusive? That's bang-your-head-against-a-wall frustrating when you're running for a Republican-leaning seat.
### **It 's all-consuming (of your time and your money)**
I have a ton of respect for [Rebecca Cooke](https://substack.com/redirect/cbf9fb57-dede-4bf1-964a-779abc113749?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),13 who ran for Congress in western Wisconsin [while waitressing](https://substack.com/redirect/710559d6-8cda-420f-b66d-24c1c5a4bab7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It is extremely difficult to work while running. Why?
* There's basically no upper bound on how much work you _could_ do: there are [760,000 people or so who live in a Congressional District](https://substack.com/redirect/9258bda6-46ac-4fcd-8d6a-2b01db8d8258?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and in theory, it's a good use of your time to talk to all of them.14
* To do the work that you need to run a campaign--meet with voters, raise money, manage press, etc.--it's borderline impossible to work a full-time job. It's hard enough to find the time just to sleep and eat.

Congressional candidates are allowed to [pay themselves a salary out of their campaign funds](https://substack.com/redirect/2d432156-ad1a-4c76-bdd1-fcf20ec56c60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). This is a good policy, one that allows people without substantial savings to run for office.
The problem is that it's used as a powerful political hit. [Ray Hartmann](https://substack.com/redirect/8054810b-d1b4-479c-b0f2-2ab705ab92b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [ran and lost against Ann Wagner](https://substack.com/redirect/fbd609ca-0986-455f-bbb8-f583357ef5fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in MO-02 and collected a salary through this run; [Wagner's campaign hit him hard for it](https://substack.com/redirect/0a67d8e5-8bc1-4bd8-88e9-635edc7ace18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).15
When you consider the views of the American public, I get it. 63% of voters say that [some or all people running for office do so to enrich themselves](https://substack.com/redirect/9c1815d9-2b27-4288-a689-bb76c614fd0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9c1815d9-2b27-4288-a689-bb76c614fd0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But no matter how much you have, running for Congress requires you to draw down on savings. **It 's a sacrifice treated as an exercise in self-enrichment, which is a tough combination.**16
Should members of Congress be barred from trading individual stocks? Absolutely. It corrodes trust, feeding into the narrative above, and it's [opposed by the overwhelming majority of Americans](https://substack.com/redirect/c84f33df-90a1-4a27-8b5d-d47743c33654?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).17 But this does nothing to help candidates, who almost always end up losing money by running for Congress.18
### **There 's a lot that's wonderful about running too**
I'm not a misanthrope and there's a lot that's uniquely rewarding about running for office too. **The ability to meet people from all walks of life --different neighborhoods, different ages, different jobs, different lived experiences--is unlike anything else you can do.**
The fun parts are meeting people who don't think about politics every day, with whom you can have interesting and nuanced conversations, even if they're not ultimately going to vote for you.
I went around to parts of the district where there weren't a lot of Democrats; I did an event at a bar in St. Charles [where I was most certainly the first political candidate to show up there](https://substack.com/redirect/03f47434-bca2-42b8-ada5-fb0c76343ae0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); I did an [online Civilization VI stream](https://substack.com/redirect/5b281a28-f5d6-498c-8329-fe66b78dbf5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to try to reach a different set of non-political people.19
**Politics is a game of addition, not subtraction** , and these sorts of efforts are critical to winning elections. But given the other constraints of running a campaign--party pressure, fundraising pressure, making it through primaries--it's tough to do.
Reaching new voters, independent voters, and I'm-not-sure-whether-I'm-going-to-vote voters usually doesn't become a priority for campaigns until close to the end, at which point most candidates have probably been running for at least a year.
### **What can we do to make it easier for people to run for office?**
There's no easy fix for this, obviously. But a few ideas for how we fix this:
* Support20 candidates like Jared Golden and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, who have a track record of winning because they understand that politics is a game of addition. There are plenty of those candidates out there, running at all levels of government, and they deserve your support.
* Don't stigmatize candidates who draw salaries from their campaign accounts. The vast, vast majority of working-age Americans can't easily take a year off to run for office--but in many cases, those are the best candidates. Within reason, we shouldn't be hitting them for supporting their families.
* As a candidate, as a party loyalist, or as a campaign volunteer, find the people who are less likely to vote, because they're busy or distrustful or whatever else. Demonstrate that you show up and that you care.
* Get off social media! This is true for candidates, voters, citizens, and just about everyone. It's pretty clearly bad for all of us...

_For press inquiries, please contact press@ben-samuels.com._
1
Trump had beaten Biden by all of [115 votes in the 2020 Presidential election](https://substack.com/redirect/839d53e2-fe68-49c1-9ee6-0e6272577caf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); by presidential vote share, it was the most competitive Congressional district in the United States that year.
2
In all likelihood we would've won the primary, and we would've faced a difficult, though winnable, general election against incumbent [Ann Wagner](https://substack.com/redirect/ff4f5e77-96b6-43a3-aad2-c979237d6da8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Wikipedia describes her as a member of the "moderate bloc of her party." That's an assessment with which I vehemently disagree. In any event, I do think she probably loathes Donald Trump, at least in private, because it's forced her into taking some nuttier positions than she'd generally like to.
3
Based on what I heard from people in Jefferson City, that was targeted at me and designed to keep me from running. I'm one of the few people I know to have been personally gerrymandered, which is about 90% frustrating and 10% flattering.
There's maybe a lesson in here about not running Congressional campaigns in a redistricting year, but [North Carolina](https://substack.com/redirect/24ce213f-912d-4552-9aa2-8bda775c2d90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Ohio](https://substack.com/redirect/3268b444-8c97-47a2-967d-a27c7a1f1757?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are doing just fine redistricting at their own cadence, so maybe you're never really safe.
4
I used this poker metaphor a lot: I was comfortable staying in the hand with an open-ended straight draw heading into the river. But I couldn't stay in when my only path to winning was hitting runner-runner aces on the turn and the river. (h/t to Jeff Smith, the [Prince](https://substack.com/redirect/2e1958a7-866f-4a93-a7f1-859499c0a943?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [of](https://substack.com/redirect/874fe354-bbd1-4751-9918-e538bfc8bdb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [Missouri](https://substack.com/redirect/7c0a41af-5301-48d2-9ee1-e68458d438f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [Political](https://substack.com/redirect/13881012-e7b4-4d46-bc14-2293cfd3e30c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [Poker](https://substack.com/redirect/6904b7a9-d0ef-4690-a7fa-20d33f30274f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [Metaphors](https://substack.com/redirect/82cdaea9-017b-4b71-b3cd-bd540f784803?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)
5
State Rep. [Trish Gunby](https://substack.com/redirect/7515e927-dfc0-4afb-b443-423c10992263?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who ultimately won a [functionally uncontested primary](https://substack.com/redirect/ac946391-775d-4123-ab9c-4283c0c2dfb3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [lost the general election by about 13%](https://substack.com/redirect/cb554d21-1d5c-481d-8821-46e4f4959911?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
6
Apparently that includes [my former boss Charlie Baker](https://substack.com/redirect/3032538e-8d03-48bd-a998-1f30e86e0246?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a guy who I admire a ton.
7
Let me be clear: I'm hardly a perfect candidate for public office! But there are lots of obstacles for nontraditional candidates of all stripes--the sorts of people who, in many cases, _do_ make the best candidates--that we need to address, or political extremism and polarization will get worse.
8
I've covered this more towards the end of my post, but there's a lot that's wonderful about it too. I don't want to create the impression that it's _all_ bad. But it's definitely tough!
9
Where people found the energy or the time to think about me that much remains, genuinely, baffling to me. I promise you, I'm not that interesting.
10
There are a bunch of different examples of this. I remember tweeting in support of President Biden, after he called [to "fund the police" in the '22 State of the Union](https://substack.com/redirect/969f6059-52e0-4a99-9f08-015f5cf0ce57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Despite it being a [hugely unpopular movement](https://substack.com/redirect/017975ff-2c08-450d-bb5a-58ed7d3e9fb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), then and now, the only vitriol was pretty stupidly unending.
Not just on this issue, but across the board: I thought the pendulum had swung too far on a bunch of different issues, and voters generally agreed with that in the 2024 election. But the loudest voices are the most extreme--entirely out of touch but with a direct line of communication through your notifications.
11
Specifically, I worked as a policy advisor for Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel (D) and Massachusetts Governor Charlie Baker (R).
12
This is true for young voters too. [The most important issue for voters under 30, by far, was jobs and the economy](https://substack.com/redirect/4126242c-779b-405c-ac22-6e1894f20b89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
13
It's no accident that in a district that [Trump won by about 8%](https://substack.com/redirect/159e7730-36f4-46ad-88eb-675addeea336?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Cooke, as a Democrat, [lost by less than 3%](https://substack.com/redirect/94ff0bb9-127f-4e15-b60a-7cf97e65cb8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
14
In practice, of course, it's lower: children, non-citizens, people you're _never_ going to win over, etc. But even then, it's still hundreds of thousands of people with whom you could be having productive conversations.
15
The fact that the _St. Louis Post-Dispatch_ covered the story as such is part of the problem, by the way. It's being treated as a bit of a scandal.
16
While I don't doubt that there are people who run for office to enrich themselves ([people I have written about before, in fact](https://substack.com/redirect/9bea8e4b-695f-48e6-b078-ef071d494653?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)), there are significantly faster, easier, and more lucrative ways to pull off a grift--[a branded meme coin](https://substack.com/redirect/3d98d6c1-04cc-4352-a04a-c2155aec3f4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), for instance.
Ultimately, I'm lucky that I could afford to run for office. But it's a tragic commentary on who's able to run for office that I even have to say that.
17
When I mention to people I meet--friends of friends, at restaurants, wherever--that I work in politics, I can't tell you how often this comes up when I mention to people that I work in politics.
Data is not the plural of anecdote, but it's consistent with my own experience: the fact that members of Congress can trade individual stocks feeds into a narrative of self-enrichment and corruption. That alone might be an argument for banning it.
18
Unfortunately, I could go on here about some of the other personal challenges of running for office. And these are basically true across the board, regardless of one's political persuasion:
* It completely erodes your sense of trust. The feeling of being in public--at a restaurant or wherever--with family or friends, looking over your shoulder to see who might be listening in on a private conversation is pretty exhausting.
* On that note, it's extremely demanding on your family. You as a candidate might sign up for this; your family did not. And they probably take things a lot more personally than you do.

And your prize for winning? You're right back in the saddle, running again almost immediately. And obviously it's pretty difficult to get laws passed in Congress these days even if you do manage to find your way to Washington.
19
Two things:
* I'd like to think that I was ahead of the curve on this one, in terms of streaming video games I play as a way of reaching lower-propensity voters.
* Shout-out to my friend Jack L., who noted (correctly) that I actually played really poorly in this livestream. I'll chalk it up to being distracted...

20
With votes, with volunteer time, or with money. Support in politics takes lots of different forms.

Feel free to share this post with someone who will find this interesting. (If you're reading this email because someone sent it to you, .) For press inquiries, please contact press@ben-samuels.com. 1 Trump had beaten Biden by all of ; by presidential vote share, it was the most competitive Congressional district in the United States that year. 2 In all likelihood we would've won the primary, and we would've faced a difficult, though winnable, general election against incumbent . Wikipedia describes her as a member of the "moderate bloc of her party." That's an assessment with which I vehemently disagree. In any event, I do think she probably loathes Donald Trump, at least in private, because it's forced her into taking some nuttier positions than she'd generally like to. 3 Based on what I heard from people in Jefferson City, that was targeted at me and designed to keep me from running. I'm one of the few people I know to have been personally gerrymandered, which is about 90% frustrating and 10% flattering. There's maybe a lesson in here about not running Congressional campaigns in a redistricting year, but and are doing just fine redistricting at their own cadence, so maybe you're never really safe. 4 I used this poker metaphor a lot: I was comfortable staying in the hand with an open-ended straight draw heading into the river. But I couldn't stay in when my only path to winning was hitting runner-runner aces on the turn and the river. (h/t to Jeff Smith, the .) 5 State Rep. , who ultimately won a , . 6 Apparently that includes , a guy who I admire a ton. 7 Let me be clear: I'm hardly a perfect candidate for public office! But there are lots of obstacles for nontraditional candidates of all stripes--the sorts of people who, in many cases, do make the best candidates--that we need to address, or political extremism and polarization will get worse. 8 I've covered this more towards the end of my post, but there's a lot that's wonderful about it too. I don't want to create the impression that it's all bad. But it's definitely tough! 9 Where people found the energy or the time to think about me that much remains, genuinely, baffling to me. I promise you, I'm not that interesting. 10 There are a bunch of different examples of this. I remember tweeting in support of President Biden, after he called . Despite it being a , then and now, the only vitriol was pretty stupidly unending. Not just on this issue, but across the board: I thought the pendulum had swung too far on a bunch of different issues, and voters generally agreed with that in the 2024 election. But the loudest voices are the most extreme--entirely out of touch but with a direct line of communication through your notifications. 11 Specifically, I worked as a policy advisor for Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel (D) and Massachusetts Governor Charlie Baker (R). 12 This is true for young voters too. . 13 It's no accident that in a district that , Cooke, as a Democrat, . 14 In practice, of course, it's lower: children, non-citizens, people you're never going to win over, etc. But even then, it's still hundreds of thousands of people with whom you could be having productive conversations. 15 The fact that the St. Louis Post-Dispatch covered the story as such is part of the problem, by the way. It's being treated as a bit of a scandal. 16 While I don't doubt that there are people who run for office to enrich themselves (), there are significantly faster, easier, and more lucrative ways to pull off a grift--, for instance. Ultimately, I'm lucky that I could afford to run for office. But it's a tragic commentary on who's able to run for office that I even have to say that. 17 When I mention to people I meet--friends of friends, at restaurants, wherever--that I work in politics, I can't tell you how often this comes up when I mention to people that I work in politics. Data is not the plural of anecdote, but it's consistent with my own experience: the fact that members of Congress can trade individual stocks feeds into a narrative of self-enrichment and corruption. That alone might be an argument for banning it. 18 Unfortunately, I could go on here about some of the other personal challenges of running for office. And these are basically true across the board, regardless of one's political persuasion: It completely erodes your sense of trust. The feeling of being in public--at a restaurant or wherever--with family or friends, looking over your shoulder to see who might be listening in on a private conversation is pretty exhausting. On that note, it's extremely demanding on your family. You as a candidate might sign up for this; your family did not. And they probably take things a lot more personally than you do. And your prize for winning? You're right back in the saddle, running again almost immediately. And obviously it's pretty difficult to get laws passed in Congress these days even if you do manage to find your way to Washington. 19 Two things: I'd like to think that I was ahead of the curve on this one, in terms of streaming video games I play as a way of reaching lower-propensity voters. * Shout-out to my friend Jack L., who noted (correctly) that I actually played really poorly in this livestream. I'll chalk it up to being distracted... 20 With votes, with volunteer time, or with money. Support in politics takes lots of different forms. | | | (C) 2025 Ben Samuels 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

| Mayor Wu Called Before Congress
---
---
| Boston, MA -Mayor Michelle Wu has been called to appear before the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, and we commend the committee for its due diligence in investigating the impact of sanctuary policies on public safety and federal immigration enforcement. Following recent U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrests in Boston--including multiple MS-13 gang members, murder and rape suspects, and a Haitian gang member with 18 prior convictions--it is more critical than ever that Mayor Wu be held accountable for policies that attract dangerous individuals to Boston and put public safety at risk.
MassGOP Chair Amy Carnevale issued the following statement:
"When speaking to her progressive supporters or friendly media outlets, Mayor Wu proudly defends her sanctuary policies, claiming they stand on solid legal ground. However, the recent ICE arrests in Boston prove beyond doubt that sanctuary policies endanger public safety. Every time the Mayor prioritizes her own pride and politics over common sense, more criminal illegal immigrants are drawn to Boston--putting Massachusetts residents at risk and forcing federal authorities to step in. If Mayor Wu truly believes in her policies, she should have no issue defending them before Congress. Bostonians deserve accountability. We call on Mayor Wu to testify and justify her extreme stance before the American people."

### ###

* **TOP NEWS**

"**Key Trump ally to decide on possible run against leading Republican in 'next couple of months',** " Fox News' **Paul Steinhauser** and**Peter Pinedo** -- "Speaking to Republican Party members in Denton County Monday night, Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** , a longtime ally of President **Donald Trump** , listed several Republicans he plans to purge from the Texas GOP for being insufficiently conservative.

Among those on Paxton's list was Texas' senior U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** , one of the most powerful members of the Senate GOP.

The crowd erupted into loud applause as Paxton said, "The second thing we need to do, and I might play a role in this, is replace John Cornyn in the U.S. Senate."

The attorney general, who worked with the Trump team to file a lawsuit in December that [successfully secured a court order](https://substack.com/redirect/ef671b17-5a90-43cd-9492-341027ef8576?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) stopping the Biden administration from continuing sales of border wall materials, has long hinted at a potential run to replace Cornyn.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/0f670f70-1f22-4780-b02b-c53ac92048b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"I can't think of a single thing he's accomplished for our state or even for the country," Paxton said in a September 2023 interview on the Fox News Channel. And pointing to a possible Senate run in 2026, Paxton said, "Somebody needs to step up and run against this guy," adding, "everything's on the table for me."

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Paxton gave more credence to the rumors, saying despite "loving what I'm doing ... I'm looking potentially at the U.S. Senate."

He shared that he is in talks with groups in Texas about a possible 2026 Senate run and will likely decide in the "next couple of months."

Paxton claimed Cornyn does not represent the conservative values of Texans and accused him of not being an ally of Trump.

He has also regularly labeled Cornyn a "RINO," a "Republican in name only" and an insult MAGA and "America First" Republicans have regularly used to criticize more mainstream or establishment members of the GOP.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/0f670f70-1f22-4780-b02b-c53ac92048b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Another source close to Paxton told Fox News Digital the attorney general "plans to spend the next few months meeting with voters, donors and grassroots activists across the state to gauge interest and decide how he can serve Texas best."

The attorney general has faced his own set of challenges. In 2022, he defeated a primary effort by [primary effort](https://substack.com/redirect/f2696036-2c47-4432-a3db-daeb03ebdffd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by former Texas Land Commissioner **George P. Bush** amid charges of bribery and corruption. In 2023, the Texas House of Representatives voted to impeach Paxton, but he was eventually acquitted of all charges by the state senate.

For his part, Cornyn, who has served in the Senate since 2002, has no intention of leaving the Senate. After serving in key GOP leadership positions, including chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, from 2009-2013, and Senate majority whip, from 2015-2019, he [threw his hat in the ring to become the Senate majority leader in 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/613cfd87-6b88-48cd-a7cb-cd8b92ad185f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), though he ultimately lost to South Dakota Sen. **John Thune**.

Cornyn, meanwhile, has said he will "absolutely" run again in 2026.

In recent months, he has also been a vocal supporter of Trump's Cabinet picks and has slammed Democrats for delaying confirmations for key positions. In a speech on the Senate floor earlier this month, he said, "Our first and most urgent task is to confirm President Trump's nominees for his Cabinet."

With both considered leading Republicans and both holding significant support, any potential primary race between the two in the Lone Star State promises to be a dramatic -- perhaps messy -- showdown.

One of the primary questions that remains is whether the president would support his longtime ally Paxton or if he would, in the interest of preserving party unity, support a GOP establishment that has previously been criticized as "weak" and "ineffective."

"The big question is whether Trump would support Paxton over Cornyn in a primary challenge," **Matt Mackowiak** , a veteran Republican strategist and communications consultant based in Texas and Washington, D.C., told Fox News Digital.

"Cornyn's never lost a race. Cornyn has a lot of support around the state. He's traveled all corners of the state for a long time and is very well known and very well liked," said Mackowiak. "We haven't had a Republican senator lose a primary since**Richard Lugar** in 2004. As much as people sometimes think it's doable, think it's easy, think it's inevitable, it really just doesn't happen. But I'm not saying it can't happen. I'm not saying that Paxton can't win. I think he certainly has a decent chance."

Mackowiak added that if Paxton runs, it "would be a massive race with national consequences."

"You'd have national activists and money involved on both sides," he said. "It could end up being one of the biggest primaries of the cycle and probably the most significant statewide primary in Texas since Dewhurst-Cruz [when former Texas Solicitor General **Ted Cruz** defeated Lt. Gov. **David Dewhurst** for the GOP Senate nomination in 2012 en route to winning his first U.S. Senate election] or it may not materialize at all. And I think it's going to be several months before we know."" TOP NEWS "Key Trump ally to decide on possible run against leading Republican in 'next couple of months', " Fox News' Paul Steinhauser andPeter Pinedo -- "Speaking to Republican Party members in Denton County Monday night, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , a longtime ally of President Donald Trump , listed several Republicans he plans to purge from the Texas GOP for being insufficiently conservative. Among those on Paxton's list was Texas' senior U.S. Sen. John Cornyn , one of the most powerful members of the Senate GOP. The crowd erupted into loud applause as Paxton said, "The second thing we need to do, and I might play a role in this, is replace John Cornyn in the U.S. Senate." The attorney general, who worked with the Trump team to file a lawsuit in December that stopping the Biden administration from continuing sales of border wall materials, has long hinted at a potential run to replace Cornyn. "I can't think of a single thing he's accomplished for our state or even for the country," Paxton said in a September 2023 interview on the Fox News Channel. And pointing to a possible Senate run in 2026, Paxton said, "Somebody needs to step up and run against this guy," adding, "everything's on the table for me." In an interview with Fox News Digital, Paxton gave more credence to the rumors, saying despite "loving what I'm doing ... I'm looking potentially at the U.S. Senate." He shared that he is in talks with groups in Texas about a possible 2026 Senate run and will likely decide in the "next couple of months." Paxton claimed Cornyn does not represent the conservative values of Texans and accused him of not being an ally of Trump. He has also regularly labeled Cornyn a "RINO," a "Republican in name only" and an insult MAGA and "America First" Republicans have regularly used to criticize more mainstream or establishment members of the GOP. Another source close to Paxton told Fox News Digital the attorney general "plans to spend the next few months meeting with voters, donors and grassroots activists across the state to gauge interest and decide how he can serve Texas best." The attorney general has faced his own set of challenges. In 2022, he defeated a primary effort by by former Texas Land Commissioner George P. Bush amid charges of bribery and corruption. In 2023, the Texas House of Representatives voted to impeach Paxton, but he was eventually acquitted of all charges by the state senate. For his part, Cornyn, who has served in the Senate since 2002, has no intention of leaving the Senate. After serving in key GOP leadership positions, including chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, from 2009-2013, and Senate majority whip, from 2015-2019, he , though he ultimately lost to South Dakota Sen. John Thune. Cornyn, meanwhile, has said he will "absolutely" run again in 2026. In recent months, he has also been a vocal supporter of Trump's Cabinet picks and has slammed Democrats for delaying confirmations for key positions. In a speech on the Senate floor earlier this month, he said, "Our first and most urgent task is to confirm President Trump's nominees for his Cabinet." With both considered leading Republicans and both holding significant support, any potential primary race between the two in the Lone Star State promises to be a dramatic -- perhaps messy -- showdown. One of the primary questions that remains is whether the president would support his longtime ally Paxton or if he would, in the interest of preserving party unity, support a GOP establishment that has previously been criticized as "weak" and "ineffective." "The big question is whether Trump would support Paxton over Cornyn in a primary challenge," Matt Mackowiak , a veteran Republican strategist and communications consultant based in Texas and Washington, D.C., told Fox News Digital. "Cornyn's never lost a race. Cornyn has a lot of support around the state. He's traveled all corners of the state for a long time and is very well known and very well liked," said Mackowiak. "We haven't had a Republican senator lose a primary sinceRichard Lugar in 2004. As much as people sometimes think it's doable, think it's easy, think it's inevitable, it really just doesn't happen. But I'm not saying it can't happen. I'm not saying that Paxton can't win. I think he certainly has a decent chance." Mackowiak added that if Paxton runs, it "would be a massive race with national consequences." "You'd have national activists and money involved on both sides," he said. "It could end up being one of the biggest primaries of the cycle and probably the most significant statewide primary in Texas since Dewhurst-Cruz [when former Texas Solicitor General Ted Cruz defeated Lt. Gov. David Dewhurst for the GOP Senate nomination in 2012 en route to winning his first U.S. Senate election] or it may not materialize at all. And I think it's going to be several months before we know."" FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. | | There has been a lot of alarming news this month. Today, I would like to share a few pieces of good news for Northwest Washington. **First, an $18 million grant to improve rail safety and reduce congestion on Everett's Smith Island:** I worked alongside Everett Mayor Cassie Franklin and the Everett business community to apply for a grant established by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to help communities eliminate dangerous highway-rail grade crossings. This month, Everett was awarded an $18,090,000 grant to construct an overpass and a new integrated roundabout near the Smith Island railroad terminal. Once completed, these improvements will make it easier and safer for first responders to address emergencies, commuters to get to and from jobs and school, and trucks and trains to transport goods to market and keep the economy moving in Northwest Washington. **Next, a RAISE Grant for Skagit Transit.** Since the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law was signed in 2022, I have been able to help secure $103.9 million in RAISE Grants for our district — this month, we brought home another **$19.5 million for Skagit Transit's maintenance, operations, and administration facility.** Thanks to the hard work of stakeholders including Skagit Transit CEO Crystle Stidham, local leaders, and members of the Skagit Transit Board of Directors, we were able to earn the funding Skagit Transit needs to continue building a better maintenance, operations, and administration facility in Burlington, and deliver on its goal of meeting the region's existing and future transportation needs. **Finally, I helped secure another $2 million RAISE Grant for the Pepin Flood, Agriculture, Safety, Salmon, and Transportation (FASST) project.** This funding will help the City of Lynden complete its relocation project of Pepin Creek, which runs in deep roadside ditches that overflow and flood the area during winter storms. This new design will allow the city to create a plan for the transportation corridor and water, sewer, stormwater infrastructure for future development. **While the Chaos Caucus continues their distractions and political theater, I am eager to continue getting real work accomplished for the people of Northwest Washington.** I know that together we can continue making meaningful progress in our communities — and these three accomplishments are only the beginning. This funding will help the City of Lynden complete its relocation project of Pepin Creek, which runs in deep roadside ditches that overflow and flood the area during winter storms. This new design will allow the city to create a plan for the transportation corridor and water, sewer, stormwater infrastructure for future development. While the Chaos Caucus continues their distractions and political theater, I am eager to continue getting real work accomplished for the people of Northwest Washington. I know that together we can continue making meaningful progress in our communities — and these three accomplishments are only the beginning. More soon. * **TOP NEWS**

"**Key Trump ally to decide on possible run against leading Republican in 'next couple of months',** " Fox News' **Paul Steinhauser** and**Peter Pinedo** -- "Speaking to Republican Party members in Denton County Monday night, Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** , a longtime ally of President **Donald Trump** , listed several Republicans he plans to purge from the Texas GOP for being insufficiently conservative.

Among those on Paxton's list was Texas' senior U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** , one of the most powerful members of the Senate GOP.

The crowd erupted into loud applause as Paxton said, "The second thing we need to do, and I might play a role in this, is replace John Cornyn in the U.S. Senate."

The attorney general, who worked with the Trump team to file a lawsuit in December that [successfully secured a court order](https://substack.com/redirect/afcf2f39-8409-439e-96f7-f290c2fbb55b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) stopping the Biden administration from continuing sales of border wall materials, has long hinted at a potential run to replace Cornyn.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/87ece60e-c445-4c27-857d-0aa8aa2323d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"I can't think of a single thing he's accomplished for our state or even for the country," Paxton said in a September 2023 interview on the Fox News Channel. And pointing to a possible Senate run in 2026, Paxton said, "Somebody needs to step up and run against this guy," adding, "everything's on the table for me."

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Paxton gave more credence to the rumors, saying despite "loving what I'm doing ... I'm looking potentially at the U.S. Senate."

He shared that he is in talks with groups in Texas about a possible 2026 Senate run and will likely decide in the "next couple of months."

Paxton claimed Cornyn does not represent the conservative values of Texans and accused him of not being an ally of Trump.

He has also regularly labeled Cornyn a "RINO," a "Republican in name only" and an insult MAGA and "America First" Republicans have regularly used to criticize more mainstream or establishment members of the GOP.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/87ece60e-c445-4c27-857d-0aa8aa2323d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Another source close to Paxton told Fox News Digital the attorney general "plans to spend the next few months meeting with voters, donors and grassroots activists across the state to gauge interest and decide how he can serve Texas best."

The attorney general has faced his own set of challenges. In 2022, he defeated a primary effort by [primary effort](https://substack.com/redirect/4eca5ea2-0710-4550-ab7f-f0bfc8080f7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by former Texas Land Commissioner **George P. Bush** amid charges of bribery and corruption. In 2023, the Texas House of Representatives voted to impeach Paxton, but he was eventually acquitted of all charges by the state senate.

For his part, Cornyn, who has served in the Senate since 2002, has no intention of leaving the Senate. After serving in key GOP leadership positions, including chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, from 2009-2013, and Senate majority whip, from 2015-2019, he [threw his hat in the ring to become the Senate majority leader in 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/229465e9-4357-4c45-bb4d-d14a9d81d26f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), though he ultimately lost to South Dakota Sen. **John Thune**.

Cornyn, meanwhile, has said he will "absolutely" run again in 2026.

In recent months, he has also been a vocal supporter of Trump's Cabinet picks and has slammed Democrats for delaying confirmations for key positions. In a speech on the Senate floor earlier this month, he said, "Our first and most urgent task is to confirm President Trump's nominees for his Cabinet."

With both considered leading Republicans and both holding significant support, any potential primary race between the two in the Lone Star State promises to be a dramatic -- perhaps messy -- showdown.

One of the primary questions that remains is whether the president would support his longtime ally Paxton or if he would, in the interest of preserving party unity, support a GOP establishment that has previously been criticized as "weak" and "ineffective."

"The big question is whether Trump would support Paxton over Cornyn in a primary challenge," **Matt Mackowiak** , a veteran Republican strategist and communications consultant based in Texas and Washington, D.C., told Fox News Digital.

"Cornyn's never lost a race. Cornyn has a lot of support around the state. He's traveled all corners of the state for a long time and is very well known and very well liked," said Mackowiak. "We haven't had a Republican senator lose a primary since**Richard Lugar** in 2004. As much as people sometimes think it's doable, think it's easy, think it's inevitable, it really just doesn't happen. But I'm not saying it can't happen. I'm not saying that Paxton can't win. I think he certainly has a decent chance."

Mackowiak added that if Paxton runs, it "would be a massive race with national consequences."

"You'd have national activists and money involved on both sides," he said. "It could end up being one of the biggest primaries of the cycle and probably the most significant statewide primary in Texas since Dewhurst-Cruz [when former Texas Solicitor General **Ted Cruz** defeated Lt. Gov. **David Dewhurst** for the GOP Senate nomination in 2012 en route to winning his first U.S. Senate election] or it may not materialize at all. And I think it's going to be several months before we know."" TOP NEWS "Key Trump ally to decide on possible run against leading Republican in 'next couple of months', " Fox News' Paul Steinhauser andPeter Pinedo -- "Speaking to Republican Party members in Denton County Monday night, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , a longtime ally of President Donald Trump , listed several Republicans he plans to purge from the Texas GOP for being insufficiently conservative. Among those on Paxton's list was Texas' senior U.S. Sen. John Cornyn , one of the most powerful members of the Senate GOP. The crowd erupted into loud applause as Paxton said, "The second thing we need to do, and I might play a role in this, is replace John Cornyn in the U.S. Senate." The attorney general, who worked with the Trump team to file a lawsuit in December that stopping the Biden administration from continuing sales of border wall materials, has long hinted at a potential run to replace Cornyn. "I can't think of a single thing he's accomplished for our state or even for the country," Paxton said in a September 2023 interview on the Fox News Channel. And pointing to a possible Senate run in 2026, Paxton said, "Somebody needs to step up and run against this guy," adding, "everything's on the table for me." In an interview with Fox News Digital, Paxton gave more credence to the rumors, saying despite "loving what I'm doing ... I'm looking potentially at the U.S. Senate." He shared that he is in talks with groups in Texas about a possible 2026 Senate run and will likely decide in the "next couple of months." Paxton claimed Cornyn does not represent the conservative values of Texans and accused him of not being an ally of Trump. He has also regularly labeled Cornyn a "RINO," a "Republican in name only" and an insult MAGA and "America First" Republicans have regularly used to criticize more mainstream or establishment members of the GOP. Another source close to Paxton told Fox News Digital the attorney general "plans to spend the next few months meeting with voters, donors and grassroots activists across the state to gauge interest and decide how he can serve Texas best." The attorney general has faced his own set of challenges. In 2022, he defeated a primary effort by by former Texas Land Commissioner George P. Bush amid charges of bribery and corruption. In 2023, the Texas House of Representatives voted to impeach Paxton, but he was eventually acquitted of all charges by the state senate. For his part, Cornyn, who has served in the Senate since 2002, has no intention of leaving the Senate. After serving in key GOP leadership positions, including chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, from 2009-2013, and Senate majority whip, from 2015-2019, he , though he ultimately lost to South Dakota Sen. John Thune. Cornyn, meanwhile, has said he will "absolutely" run again in 2026. In recent months, he has also been a vocal supporter of Trump's Cabinet picks and has slammed Democrats for delaying confirmations for key positions. In a speech on the Senate floor earlier this month, he said, "Our first and most urgent task is to confirm President Trump's nominees for his Cabinet." With both considered leading Republicans and both holding significant support, any potential primary race between the two in the Lone Star State promises to be a dramatic -- perhaps messy -- showdown. One of the primary questions that remains is whether the president would support his longtime ally Paxton or if he would, in the interest of preserving party unity, support a GOP establishment that has previously been criticized as "weak" and "ineffective." "The big question is whether Trump would support Paxton over Cornyn in a primary challenge," Matt Mackowiak , a veteran Republican strategist and communications consultant based in Texas and Washington, D.C., told Fox News Digital. "Cornyn's never lost a race. Cornyn has a lot of support around the state. He's traveled all corners of the state for a long time and is very well known and very well liked," said Mackowiak. "We haven't had a Republican senator lose a primary sinceRichard Lugar in 2004. As much as people sometimes think it's doable, think it's easy, think it's inevitable, it really just doesn't happen. But I'm not saying it can't happen. I'm not saying that Paxton can't win. I think he certainly has a decent chance." Mackowiak added that if Paxton runs, it "would be a massive race with national consequences." "You'd have national activists and money involved on both sides," he said. "It could end up being one of the biggest primaries of the cycle and probably the most significant statewide primary in Texas since Dewhurst-Cruz [when former Texas Solicitor General Ted Cruz defeated Lt. Gov. David Dewhurst for the GOP Senate nomination in 2012 en route to winning his first U.S. Senate election] or it may not materialize at all. And I think it's going to be several months before we know."" FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. Don't miss out on the fastest-growing daily newsletter in Texas – join a thriving community that values accurate, relevant news delivered straight to your inbox every morning. | TOP NEWS “Key Trump ally to decide on possible run against leading Republican in 'next couple of months',” Fox News' Paul Steinhauser andPeter Pinedo — “Speaking to Republican Party members in Denton County Monday night, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , a longtime ally of President Donald Trump , listed several Republicans he plans to purge from the Texas GOP for being insufficiently conservative. Among those on Paxton’s list was Texas’ senior U.S. Sen. John Cornyn , one of the most powerful members of the Senate GOP. The crowd erupted into loud applause as Paxton said, "The second thing we need to do, and I might play a role in this, is replace John Cornyn in the U.S. Senate." The attorney general, who worked with the Trump team to file a lawsuit in December that stopping the Biden administration from continuing sales of border wall materials, has long hinted at a potential run to replace Cornyn. » "I can’t think of a single thing he’s accomplished for our state or even for the country," Paxton said in a September 2023 interview on the Fox News Channel. And pointing to a possible Senate run in 2026, Paxton said, "Somebody needs to step up and run against this guy," adding, "everything’s on the table for me." In an interview with Fox News Digital, Paxton gave more credence to the rumors, saying despite "loving what I’m doing ... I’m looking potentially at the U.S. Senate." He shared that he is in talks with groups in Texas about a possible 2026 Senate run and will likely decide in the "next couple of months." Paxton claimed Cornyn does not represent the conservative values of Texans and accused him of not being an ally of Trump. He has also regularly labeled Cornyn a "RINO," a "Republican in name only" and an insult MAGA and "America First" Republicans have regularly used to criticize more mainstream or establishment members of the GOP. » Another source close to Paxton told Fox News Digital the attorney general "plans to spend the next few months meeting with voters, donors and grassroots activists across the state to gauge interest and decide how he can serve Texas best." The attorney general has faced his own set of challenges. In 2022, he defeated a primary effort by by former Texas Land Commissioner George P. Bush amid charges of bribery and corruption. In 2023, the Texas House of Representatives voted to impeach Paxton, but he was eventually acquitted of all charges by the state senate. For his part, Cornyn, who has served in the Senate since 2002, has no intention of leaving the Senate. After serving in key GOP leadership positions, including chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, from 2009-2013, and Senate majority whip, from 2015-2019, he , though he ultimately lost to South Dakota Sen. John Thune. Cornyn, meanwhile, has said he will "absolutely" run again in 2026. In recent months, he has also been a vocal supporter of Trump’s Cabinet picks and has slammed Democrats for delaying confirmations for key positions. In a speech on the Senate floor earlier this month, he said, "Our first and most urgent task is to confirm President Trump's nominees for his Cabinet." With both considered leading Republicans and both holding significant support, any potential primary race between the two in the Lone Star State promises to be a dramatic — perhaps messy — showdown. One of the primary questions that remains is whether the president would support his longtime ally Paxton or if he would, in the interest of preserving party unity, support a GOP establishment that has previously been criticized as "weak" and "ineffective." "The big question is whether Trump would support Paxton over Cornyn in a primary challenge," Matt Mackowiak , a veteran Republican strategist and communications consultant based in Texas and Washington, D.C., told Fox News Digital. "Cornyn’s never lost a race. Cornyn has a lot of support around the state. He’s traveled all corners of the state for a long time and is very well known and very well liked," said Mackowiak. "We haven’t had a Republican senator lose a primary sinceRichard Lugar in 2004. As much as people sometimes think it’s doable, think it’s easy, think it’s inevitable, it really just doesn’t happen. But I’m not saying it can’t happen. I’m not saying that Paxton can’t win. I think he certainly has a decent chance." Mackowiak added that if Paxton runs, it "would be a massive race with national consequences." "You’d have national activists and money involved on both sides," he said. "It could end up being one of the biggest primaries of the cycle and probably the most significant statewide primary in Texas since Dewhurst-Cruz [when former Texas Solicitor General Ted Cruz defeated Lt. Gov. David Dewhurst for the GOP Senate nomination in 2012 en route to winning his first U.S. Senate election] or it may not materialize at all. body:
Over the next four years, we need to be louder about defending our rights and keep up the good fight regardless of the Trump Administration’s attempts to exhaust us. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/101183645/525174230/-785282667?refcode=AU_RAB_FR_GEN_EOM_AC_20250129_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4NDJmYTNkZS02YWRlLWVmMTEtODhmOC0wMDIyNDgyYTk1NzkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5bWgXTHJiDHWfDkTe3Irf_fPj-TOYkLGv_Stn2z9CTc=)

Hey Peter, I know it feels impossible to escape the constant headlines on President Trump’s latest unconstitutional attacks on vulnerable communities. These are scary times, no doubt. But no matter who the president is and no matter how divided Congress is — _we must face these challenges and attacks with courage and clarity._ I’m ready to do the work to protect our Constitution and strengthen our delicate democracy. I’ll be working tirelessly to address the urgent needs of Vermonters and working people across America. **How we do this work matters, too.** I’ll be advocating for real change and calling out any attempt to slide our country toward authoritarianism. I refuse to let any attempt to harm our fundamental freedoms be swept under the rug. Over the next four years, we need to be louder about defending our rights and keep up the good fight regardless of the Trump Administration’s attempts to exhaust us. **I’ll always do everything I can to stand by Vermont and our fundamental freedoms. Trump is not interested in us, our families, or our communities.

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20250129-1?refcode=em20250129-1722&amount=5&refcode2=1722_21716_xH67cr&akid=1722%2E21716%2ExH67cr)
We are witnessing a dangerous consolidation of power with one clear goal: the absolute abuse of it to settle personal grievances and to line the pockets of the uber wealthy.
The decision to freeze all federal grant and loan funds will have devastating consequences for millions. Throughout yesterday, the White House either wouldn’t or couldn’t confirm whether Medicaid — which covers nearly 1 in 5 Americans — would be impacted by the freeze. Either they don’t care if people have coverage or they don’t want people to have coverage.
**While a federal judge has temporarily halted this illegal and unconstitutional order, there is no version of this power grab that won't hurt Americans. Trump is not interested in us, our families, or our communities. Unless you donate millions of dollars or stage an insurrection, this White House just doesn’t care about you.**
But while he and his administration work to fleece the American people, I’m working in Congress to _actually_ make life more affordable for our neighbors in Delaware and workers across the country.

That is why we opened Camp Elah in the heart of Washington, D.C., just blocks away from the Supreme Court. Our mission is for **CAMP ELAH **to minister to our nation's leaders and policy makers!
---

Hi Peter, We are just over one week removed from the inauguration of Donald Trump, and I have been laser-focused on working with school board leaders, superintendents, nonprofits, and labor unions in AZ-03 to protect our community from Trump’s cruel policies.

Instead of attending Donald Trump’s inauguration last Monday, I spent the day in the Third District, volunteering at St. Vincent de Paul and honoring Martin Luther King, Jr. Day with my constituents.

Dr. King’s legacy teaches us that fighting for justice is hard work, and threats to justice anywhere are a threat to justice everywhere.

As we were working on the ground to uplift members of our community, Donald Trump signed executive order after executive order to attack immigrant communities nationwide and decimate the rights of millions of Americans.

**Donald Trump’s priorities are clear, and so are mine.**

My team and I are continuing to work hard to prepare our fight against cruel and dehumanizing immigration policies from Donald Trump and the GOP. We need comprehensive immigration reform that respects the humanity and dignity of those seeking to build a life in this country.

My district sent me to Congress to fight for our community — including the many immigrants and mixed-status families who call our district home. **[If you’re in this fight with me, can I count on your support today? | | Dear Peter, C.S. Lewis was a master at addressing life's most important questions through vivid language that is delightful and captivating to read.

His signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired countless skeptics to become believers and even more believers to renew and deepen their faith--making him the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

To help you learn more about Lewis, we produced "[**C.S. Lewis on Christianity,**](http://links.standingstrongamerica.com/u/click?_t=29c3b6e742c849fabbcc130432510e66&_m=9ed753806c064e568fd033397ed5591c&_e=tMdRsg9BeydT7JC16x3OVnLjRXsHvDcBSbJL1u7bhFpu6P4wqpafmk6cfOlHS9HLFinR9CNh3A4M0aNIpnsM2xFqw-YzbGZuyOa_Dp2i5CD9rqTs762eACrC6mktRavxvhGSGS-y00cFmHINYsAjnlaUMxM9V9O9Iv9Bu4O_hy6xs-pZOW7hF2630Ubud2G11vK7a0sKzfQDOQvyBCUG236Gc6TMfdTSZ9HD9Js5_E1wMeKz6SlOf2pZWP7wd3aepvf9zVHB-sZfhNaGHrZQ81Z7tF7JfkRUN4BhKGUCAANaH5v84PVaP9UUPE5kfnqQyinfNg-5T0Y71x_q6p6hx2xxlPcYeb2oe3M_MGkSrMm8sWnG-ZcpvFheqygpzUl6VYPHm9yl4jKmGmYk8dCjEOY65T4IeFYyfoWsKhvkhSZYVWSwETncK9qi7KmiY8y7)" which you can now own on DVD.

| | In this course you will learn Lewis's profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* good and evil,
* conversion and faith,
* prayer and the Bible,
* suffering and death,
* heaven and hell, and much more.

The instructor, Dr. Michael Ward, is a Distinguished Visiting Professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He is the author of _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis 's The Abolition of Man_, and the co-editor of _The Cambridge Companion to C.S. Lewis_. He even spent three years living in Lewis's Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!

This course is especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis's beautiful writings about faith and traces Lewis's own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for us to grow in our knowledge and understanding of Christianity.

That's why I hope you'll join us in examining the eternal questions of Christianity with C.S. Lewis with [this beautiful DVD box set](http://links.standingstrongamerica.com/u/click?_t=29c3b6e742c849fabbcc130432510e66&_m=9ed753806c064e568fd033397ed5591c&_e=tMdRsg9BeydT7JC16x3OVnLjRXsHvDcBSbJL1u7bhFpu6P4wqpafmk6cfOlHS9HLFinR9CNh3A4M0aNIpnsM2xFqw-YzbGZuyOa_Dp2i5CD9rqTs762eACrC6mktRavxvhGSGS-y00cFmHINYsAjnlaUMxM9V9O9Iv9Bu4O_hy6xs-pZOW7hF2630Ubud2G11vK7a0sKzfQDOQvyBCUG236Gc6TMfdTSZ9HD9Js5_E1wMeKz6SlOf2pZWP7wd3aepvf9zVHB-sZfhNaGHrZQ82EuuAlLGkljITFytUe3yYYGc1Yj955a2hww6CRIj8o8k4NTLoI-zlYDOQxgWNn9RD5xsyMp6IqIL2s_CSZrT2kcBos2Z0q0LXs1-m5Bast9HJw_gaSlfxA9oMr5sG6yvXMFb742ZpO_IqgejjTrVC1ZrM8p0XibsyhzbgbMboV4).

Best regards,

Peter, This is Kelly Johnson, Speaker Mike Johnson's wife. Every day since he was elected by Republicans to be Speaker of the House, Mike has been playing the role of night owl and early bird. | Peter,

In just one week, Donald Trump has launched a full-scale attack on the progress we’ve made for affordable healthcare. On Monday, he signed an executive order reversing a vital initiative by President Biden that tested ways to lower prescription drug prices and expanded access to cutting-edge cell and gene therapies for Medicaid recipients.

As a doctor for over twenty years, I worked to improve the availability and affordability of health care for my patients, and I saw firsthand the heartbreak families felt when they struggled to afford the medications they needed. In Congress, I’ve always fought for affordable healthcare because I believe that no one should have to suffer due to skyrocketing drug prices or lack of access to care.

body:

---
| |
---
| | Dear Fellow Believer, It may seem a little early to be talking about Easter, but it's really only about 12 weeks away.And in that short amount of time, my friends at Brave Books are spearheading a massive "Prepare the Way" campaign to shift the focus of Easter from bunnies and chocolate......to Jesus.And this revival mission needs you! My friend, if you've seen me talking about Brave Books on Fox News, you know their mission is to counter the ungodly lies being pushed by the Left in schools, libraries, and Hollywood......by creating high-quality, wholesome, and Godly books and entertainment that instill conservative values and Gospel lessons in our children. And their "Prepare the Way" revival campaign is their biggest effort yet to point parents and children to the empty tomb and God’s redeeming love.Here’s exactly what their strategy is...First... Brave Books knows that families need an easy and impactful way to counter the Left's secularization of Easter and instead, captivate children with its true meaning. So, they created _Saving the Easter Bunny_ , a brand-new children's book that's destined to be a classic.In it, Ronnie the Rabbit learns the hard way what sin is and that our Lord Jesus Christ loves us so much that he took the punishment for that sin.Jesus is represented by a powerful lion named Lord Joshua and the book beautifully portrays his resurrection and God's never-ending redeeming love for us. It's incredible.And let me tell you, parents are hungry for content like this because everywhere they turn godlessness is being pushed by schools, left-wing publishers like Scholastic, and Hollywood. When Brave Books first introduced a God-centered Christmas game called "_Mouse in the House_ ," to counter the secular elf game that has become so popular -- it sold out in THREE HOURS!That's why step one of Brave Books' 12-week "Prepare the Way" revival, is ramping up the printing and distribution of _Saving the Easter Bunny_ big-time. **[And today I'm hoping you'll help them kick it into high gear before orders start pouring in by rushing back your best "Prepare the Way" gift.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=cbaaf3c5319444fab5b543672d7d940c&_e=POgjwh7_pR1xlr6nWoXShJV2K8O1cDB5F9mWmT1gYeH4G4vemYQHuStz8hWjPVivCWABAMRrCzdLJIWOkOh8pP51O1RJVMhaal84SFBjhN0vP_5jJFVpmuXR4bWwrL-bvyONSjhkuZ57Dfl8in7pskdL-QjPcwI9rXM5EqRhRx6pXfvDUtC7y4rsxhoAL-QjhfzhZiKsiJS2FgQZh2XbA_GfOTosxaxOD-Jlmmva5xAHo8t7KWQzasc89jc28zO9-b1BfAuRL1s_9bQtMuELS_m6UlThJ5kZnntX6lOnoD1y4oI6RyP8GdblyIl3QO1VHfMJtJV-DOBuWdRawd9zjLyEDi7J3klOOeqKsgk7aIfePGGXA_tfdOTnuASm_cOz)** No family should go without this wonderful book because of overwhelming demand. Second... Recognizing that families who want to raise their children with wholesome Christian values often feel alone in their mission...Brave Books is launching a 17-city traveling church tour that starts in Ponta Vedra Beach, Florida and ends in Laurel, Mississippi. I'll be leading the tour in every city as we prepare our hearts and our families for Easter through prayer, worship, music, and just some good old-fashioned conversation about raising Godly children in our godless culture.Our church tour aims to ignite a spirit of revival in thousands of families this Easter season and I can't wait to see what God makes of that! But getting our worship teams, musicians, and all the rest to 17 different cities for thousands of families to enjoy won't be easy and it won't be inexpensive.But I know we can do it.Brave Books is a small Christian company founded by a doctor named Trent Talbot. After having his first child, he saw how the Left was using books and entertainment to turn the hearts and minds of America's children away from God. And so he decided to take action and with the help of believers just like you, look at what they've already done:
---
>>> They've countered the Left's radical and ungodly "Drag Queen Story Hours" and filled children's hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God with their highly-publicized "See You at the Library" campaign. Armed with Brave Books' "See You at the Library" kits, thousands of parents, grandparents, children, and concerned citizens have gathered at over 360 libraries in 49 states to take back our libraries.>>> Created an historic TV show called "Adventures with Iggy and Mr. Kirk" to fight the ungodly lessons coming out of Hollywood. It's our modern day "Mr. Rogers' Neighborhood" funded by everyday Americans who want to return American culture to God. "Adventures with Iggy and Mr. Kirk" uses humor and storytelling to reinforce the traditional biblical values that have made America great.>>> And now you are crucial to the success and failure of our "Prepare the Way" revival campaign which features the printing and distribution of _Saving the Easter Bunny_ and a 17-city church tour.

---|---|---|---

### Urgent Senate Update: Standing Up for our Federal Workers & Critical Community Investments
In the week since Donald Trump's inauguration, he has issued a flurry of dangerous executive orders to remake our nation in his image. He pardoned the rioters who bloodied and bludgeoned police officers on January 6th, rolled back initiatives to lower drug prices, commenced an all-out attack on our federal workforce, and most recently announced an attempt to illegally withhold federal grant funds from local communities. This chaotic first week focused on targeting critical services people depend on, not helping the American people. **As President Trump levies these attacks on our federal workforce and important federal investments, I want to hear from you on what impact these actions are having on priorities in your community. Hearing your stories will help us fight back - [share with us here.](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15422.42868701.6890305.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fshare-how-president-trumps-executive-orders-are-impacting-you-or-your-family&redir_log=08840167418772)** On Monday night, Trump's Office of Management and Budget [demanded](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15422.42868701.6890305.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fChrisVanHollen%2fstatus%2f1884242371652771967&redir_log=393591994293332) agencies "temporarily pause all activities related to obligation or disbursement of all Federal financial assistance." In other words, they threatened to cancel critical resources directed to our communities. In response to a massive public outcry, the Administration seems to have backed down and rescinded this memo on Wednesday afternoon. But we're by no means in the clear. This scope of the order was both broad and ambiguous - meaning it would have [impacted everything](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15422.42868701.6890305.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fChrisVanHollen%2fstatus%2f1884394320179937386&redir_log=713841008863332) from the support we provide our firefighters and first responders, to assistance to victims of domestic violence, to efforts to remove lead from our water, to initiatives to improve the health of the Chesapeake Bay. That's just a few of the many harmful local impacts we would have seen.

Make no mistake - the Trump Administration's attempt to withhold and threaten to cancel these funds is an illegal abuse of power. The president cannot suspend funding that has been duly approved by the Congress and enacted into law without Congressional approval. That blatantly defies Article I of the Constitution and the checks and balances built into our constitutional framework. [The president does not have the power to cherry-pick from the law and implement the provisions he likes while discarding those he doesn't](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15422.42868701.6890305.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvideo%2ftranscript-van-hollen-questions-vought-nominee-for-omb-director-on-federal-workforce-protections-congressional-power-of-the-purse&redir_log=075635990661332).

While the Administration may no longer be pushing the requirements under the OMB memo, many critical investments remain frozen through Trump's executive orders. And while the extent of these orders isn't clear, what is absolutely clear is that they are sowing chaos and confusion. These actions are hurting our nation - and they aren't doing anything to improve government efficiency and tackle rising costs. We must remain vigilant and continue to call out the abuses of this Administration everywhere we see them.

Trump is not only going after the federal funding that supports critical public services - he's also going after the federal civil servants who help deliver those services to the American people day in and day out. Trump has taken every opportunity to [attack our federal workforce](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15422.42868701.6890305.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fChrisVanHollen%2fstatus%2f1882178195929350191&redir_log=157342232363332) throughout the country and across Maryland - with his words and executive orders. Most disturbing is his so-called "Schedule F" plan to convert over 50,000 merit-based civil service positions into political positions and his dubious offer of "buy-outs" to encourage experienced employees to resign. This will destroy our merit-based civil service system and replace it with one based on political cronyism. It means that rather than hiring individuals based on their qualifications, experience, and knowledge, they will be selected based on a political loyalty test. This isn't just bad news for federal workers, it's bad news for every American who depends on their work. Americans don't want political hacks making decisions regarding food safety, public health, and more. They don't want these critical positions to be filled based on political loyalty rather than merit. Donald Trump's action will destroy in the next few months what it took America over a century to build: a merit-based civil service that hires the best people to do their jobs. This will open the door to widespread corruption. And, to make matters worse, President Trump has already illegally fired Inspectors General whose job it is to blow the whistle on fraud, waste, and abuse. That way, there will be no one to hold him and the political cronies installed in these agencies accountable.

Since these actions were announced, I've heard from constituents across Maryland alarmed by their impacts and trying to figure out the extent of the damage. They are facing uncertainty and confusion. With MAGA Republicans in control of both houses of Congress, our best recourse in the short term will be in the courts. We have already seen lawsuits filed by the National Treasury Employees Union, the American Federation of Government Employees, the AFSCME, and others. I wholeheartedly back the legal efforts these unions, states, and others are undertaking, and I will do all I can to support them. And every day, I will continue working to shine a light on the harm this Administration is already inflicting on the country and, wherever I can, to stop it. Onwards, Chris Van Hollen

---
---
**Here’s what I stand for:****
** ✅**Defending Our Freedoms** – From reproductive rights to voting rights, I will never stop fighting for the fundamental liberties that make America strong.
✅ **Protecting Public Education** – Our kids deserve fully funded schools, not political agendas in their classrooms and cafeterias.
✅ **Fighting for Working Families** – No Floridian should struggle to afford housing, healthcare, or a living wage while billionaires get tax breaks.
✅ **Standing Up to Gun Violence** – We need common-sense gun laws that protect our communities, not policies that put our children at risk. The stakes couldn’t be higher. Project 2025, extremist bans, and efforts to erode our democracy are real threats—but together, we can stop them. With your support, we will send a fighter to Congress who puts people first.
